scope: Primary-source reviewed native desktop ports and static recompilations for console/handheld-origin games; 13 target rows across seven public repositories.

projects.title: PokéRecomp: Pokémon FireRed Native PC Port
projects.status: Playable, according to the project README; v2.1.3 was published 2026-10-14.
projects.summary: The shared PokeRecomp launcher compiles the pret FireRed C source for x86 and links an SDL2 platform layer. The README marks FireRed playable. The player supplies a ROM; the README also notes that included decompilation data remains copyrighted and is not covered by the port code license.
projects.strategy: Decompilation-based source port: compiles pret C game source for x86 and links an SDL2 native platform layer; this is not static recompilation of a retail binary.
projects.subtype: Shared multi-game PC port; each row represents a separately named GBA/GBC target.

projects.title: CTR Native: Crash Team Racing PC Port
projects.platform: PlayStation → Windows x86 and Linux x86
projects.status: Beta 7.1 release available (published 2026-07-07); README documents native Windows and Linux builds.
projects.summary: A native PC port of the 1999 PlayStation game built on the CTR-ModSDK decompilation. Decompiled game source is compiled for Windows and Linux behind a native SDL3/platform layer; the player supplies the supported NTSC-U disc image.
projects.strategy: Decompilation-based native source port; compiles the reconstructed game source for x86 and replaces PlayStation platform services with a host layer.
projects.subtype: Native desktop port based on CTR-ModSDK; raw NTSC-U BIN disc input is required.

projects.title: ReRAC: Ratchet & Clank Native PC Rewrite
projects.platform: PlayStation 2 → macOS Apple Silicon (tested); Windows build (experimental, untested)
projects.status: Early active development; the README says all levels load and render but the project is not yet playable from start to finish. v0.3.4-alpha released 2026-10-15.
projects.summary: A Rust/Bevy native rewrite of Ratchet & Clank (2002) that ports game systems to a desktop runtime rather than emulating the PS2. Players supply the supported NTSC-U disc. The project says it is still incomplete and its launcher has not yet been released.
projects.strategy: Native source reimplementation in Rust/Bevy; game systems run on the host, with no emulator in the execution path.
projects.subtype: Early desktop rewrite; supported disc is NTSC-U SCUS-97199.

projects.title: MGB64: GoldenEye 007 Decompilation and Native PC Port
projects.platform: Nintendo 64 → macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64, and Linux x86-64
projects.status: Discontinued and unmaintained, per the README; v0.4.0-alpha.3 is the latest listed release. The README reports all 20 single-player levels boot, play, and reach mission-complete.
projects.summary: An independent portable-C decompilation and native source port of the 1997 N64 game. It uses a native platform layer for video, audio, input, timing, and saves, and requires the player’s own legally dumped ROM. The project is archived.
projects.strategy: Decompilation-based native source port; reconstructed game code runs with a dedicated desktop platform layer, not as a static binary recompilation.
projects.subtype: Archived multi-platform GoldenEye source port; the repository marks itself discontinued.

projects.title: OpenJam: NBA Jam: On Fire Edition Native PC Recompilation
projects.status: v1.0 release published 2026-09-26; README reports the recompiled game boots to gameplay and published PS3-format mods install and play. It also lists unresolved graphics/runtime rough edges.
projects.summary: A ReXGlue-based static recompilation of the Xbox 360 XBLA edition to a native Windows program. The README says the PowerPC game code is translated ahead of time to C++, and the repository contains no game files; the player supplies their legally acquired copy.
projects.strategy: Static recompilation of Xbox 360 PowerPC code to native C++ through ReXGlue, with a native Windows runtime.
projects.subtype: Xbox 360 XBLA static recompilation; README notes the Windows build also serves as a reference for a possible original-Xbox port.

projects.title: Advanced Daisenryaku Mega Drive Native Windows Port
projects.platform: Sega Mega Drive / Genesis → Windows x64
projects.status: Experimental development build. The README reports the logo, menus, tactical battles, campaigns, saves, and controller paths are partly implemented; it explicitly says full-game equivalence is not established and some boundaries, audio commands, player-two input, and campaign flow remain incomplete.
projects.summary: A native Windows reconstruction of the Mega Drive strategy game using statically translated game logic in C/C++, with ROM differential tests and no runtime 68000 interpreter. The README describes ongoing work, selected visual comparisons rather than full equivalence, and requires a user-supplied ROM.
projects.strategy: Static translation/recompilation of Mega Drive 68000 code into C/C++ with a native Win32/Direct2D/DirectWrite/XAudio2 host layer.
projects.subtype: Experimental PC port of the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis target; full-game behavioral equivalence is unverified.

projects.title: Mister Mosquito Native Windows Recompilation
projects.status: Early work in progress; the README reports title, menus, and the first stage working with sound on Vulkan. No release yet.
projects.summary: A game-specific native Windows port that translates the PS2 MIPS program to C++ and runs it against the ps2-port-engine host runtime. The project README reports booting the title, menus, and first stage with sound, widescreen, and up to 4× PS2 resolution. It contains no game code or assets; a user-owned NTSC-U SLUS-20375 disc image is required.
projects.strategy: Static translation/recompilation of PlayStation 2 MIPS code into C++ with the game's platform runtime hosted natively on Windows.
projects.subtype: PS2-to-Windows static code translation; early playable bring-up with no public release yet.
